key_insight: Oxygen vacancy formation energies in binary main-group metal oxides are largely explained by crystal reduction potential and band gap, linking vacancy energetics to cation reducibility.
engineering_relevance: Bulk-property estimates could accelerate oxide screening for energy technologies, though this study does not directly evaluate solar-cell performance.
method: Surveyed 39 oxide polymorphs across groups 1, 2, 13, 14, and 15 using r²SCAN density functional theory.
Used ShakeNBreak to locate reconstructed neutral oxygen-vacancy ground states.
Fit an interpretable model using crystal reduction potential and band gap.
evidence_signal: Calculated formation energies span 8 eV, and the two-descriptor model achieves a held-out mean absolute error of 0.31 eV.
watch_item: Predictions require caution where defect electrons are accommodated through mechanisms other than cation reduction; charged vacancies were not assessed.
paper_title: Periodic Trends in Oxygen Vacancy Formation Energies Across Binary Main-Group Metal Oxides
